WhatsApp is developing a new feature that will let users connect third-party AI agents to the app, allowing them to converse with these agents and instruct them to perform tasks on their behalf. Here are the details.

WhatsApp is developing third-party agent support

When OpenClaw and similar platforms first surged in popularity, one of the main ways users interacted with agents remotely was by connecting them to instant messaging apps.

However, many users subsequently discovered that setting up bots on WhatsApp to converse with third-party AI agents could result in their WhatsApp accounts being banned.

Meanwhile, Telegram has ridden this wave to become one of the primary platforms where users converse with or issue commands to agents running locally on their computers or in the cloud.

Now, according to WABetaInfo, WhatsApp is developing native support for third-party AI agents through a new feature that will let users connect agents directly to dedicated conversations within the app.

After a user sets up a new bot in WhatsApp, the app will generate an API key, which the user can subsequently use to connect an agent to the conversation. As WABetaInfo explains: "the specific steps vary by platform, but most services have a field where users can paste" that API key, allowing them to begin conversing with the third-party agent directly through WhatsApp.

Here's the explanation from WABetaInfo:

The site noted that the new feature is currently only available to some Android users, but is expected to roll out more widely in the near term. WABetaInfo stated that WhatsApp's implementation supports connecting up to five agents per account, and allows users to customise each agent's name and avatar. However, conversations with third-party agents are not currently end-to-end encrypted.
